metadata.note: The 'Old Put': New York City and Northern Railroad (opened 1880/81) -> New York and Northern Railway (1887) -> New York and Putnam Railroad, leased to the New York Central & Hudson River from Feb 1, 1894 and run as its Putnam Division until the last passenger train on May 29, 1958. Single track from the Harlem River through central Westchester to Brewster, with the Getty Square (Yonkers) branch 1888-1943 and a Manhattan terminal at 155th Street until 1918. Built from research/branches/new_york_and_putnam_railroad.txt (status ready, researched 2026-10-19), drawing exactly its drawable: spans. Features are split by operator per Rule 4 (NYC&N 1881-1887, NY&N 1887-1894, NYC 1894 on; the 1913/14 merger is not a split) and the NYC main line is split again at the 1931 Pocantico relocation so no pre-1931 year is drawn on the 1931 route.
sources: branchline.uk Fowler, New York State Railroads (1), sec. 3 'New York - Brewster (NYC)' and sec. 4 'Yonkers Branch'
Putnam County Historian, 'A Guide to the Old Put' (2010)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) route relation 1376423 'Putnam Branch' and 1376421 'Yonkers Branch' (old_railway_operator=NYC), their member rail-trails, and ways found with old_railway_operator~NYC in bbox (40.82,-73.95,41.43,-73.60)
OpenHistoricalMap 'Northern R.R.' (start_date 1881) ways at University Heights - Kingsbridge, folded into the routing graph
OSM Metro-North Hudson Line centreline, offset 25 m, for the schematic Sedgwick Ave - University Heights leg only
omitted: [3] Original East View trestle alignment (drawable 1881-1881 [ANCHOR], optional): FOLDED INTO the 1881-1887 feature rather than drawn. Trains crossed an 80-ft, c.1,205-ft wooden trestle over the valley later flooded as the Tarrytown Reservoir until the Pocantico Hills bypass opened Nov 26, 1881 (abandonedrails says 1882 - conflict). The NYC&N feature draws 1881 on the bypass; that is a LATER alignment than the first months of 1881. OSM relation 12946699 'New York City & Northern' (end_date 1881) maps fragments of the trestle route and could be used if the anchor is ever drawn.
[8] Mahopac Falls / Mahopac Mines Branch (Baldwin Place - Mahopac Falls): drawable NONE - no dated passenger evidence. OSM relation 1376435 exists if a source turns up.
[9] Mohansic Branch (Yorktown Heights - Mohansic State Hospital site): drawable NONE - construction/freight spur, never carried passengers (Rule 1).
The Dec 3, 1880 inaugural special (optional [ANCHOR] 1880-1880): not drawn, per the report's recommendation.
All post-May 29, 1958 main-line use and post-April 2, 1959 Lake Mahopac - Brewster use: freight only (Rule 1).
not_yet_sourced: Exact opening day of regular Brewster service (April 1881 is secondary; The Sun confirms trains at High Bridge May 1, 1881).
Month of the 1887 NY&N reorganization; day of the 1894 lease (Feb 1 from xydexx only).
155th St stub end year 1918 rests on Wikipedia's station table and Fowler's 'cl.1918'; a dated IRT Ninth Avenue extension story would confirm.
Trestle bypass: 1881 (Wikipedia, bypass stations Nov 26, 1881) vs 1882 (abandonedrails).
Start of Harlem Division 'around the horn' running over Lake Mahopac - Brewster; its April 2, 1959 end is single-source (Wikipedia).
Getty Square end: NYT June 30, 1943 taken over Fowler's '1942'.
Croton Lake crossing: whether the 1881-1905 approaches differ visibly from the 1905 bridge alignment drawn.
All headways and speeds are estimates; the only timetable consulted is the partly legible Nov 1951 Official Guide Table 90.
Exact positions of the 155th Street and Getty Square terminals, and of the Putnam's own tracks between Sedgwick Avenue and University Heights.

metadata.geocode_check: Nominatim was tried for station names and was unreliable - 'East View, NY' returned East View, West Virginia (586 km off), 'Saw Mill River' a river 7.9 km off, 'Van Cortlandt' the park (1.1 km), 'Dunwoodie' and 'Nepperhan' neighbourhood centroids 2.4/1.9 km off, Ardsley/Elmsford village polygons. Every routing waypoint was therefore pinned to a coordinate on the OSM relation itself.

properties.line: New York City and Northern: 155th Street – Brewster
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, unsourced as a figure: single-track suburban/through local line, c.52 mi in a little over two hours on the Nov 1951 Official Guide Table 90 times (partly legible OCR); not computed from a full schedule.
properties.geometry_source: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap (ODbL): the members of OSM route relation 1376423 'Putnam Branch' (old_railway_operator=NYC, named from the 1917 Moody's Manual) - South County Trailway, North County Trailway, Putnam Trailway, Putnam Greenway (Van Cortlandt Park) and the razed/abandoned Putnam Branch ways - routed waypoint to waypoint with opstrace.py (cost-weighted Dijkstra over OSM rail + rail-trails + OpenHistoricalMap), then Douglas-Peucker 8 m and trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 53.9 mi 155th Street - Putnam Junction against documented c.52 mi (Fowler: Putnam Jct 52.0 from 155th St; The Sun 1880: '51 miles from the Harlem River'; Wikipedia's station table gives Putnam Jct 53.82). APPROXIMATED LEG, 155th Street - Sedgwick Avenue (0.3 mi): straight line across the Harlem River on the line of the demolished Putnam Bridge; neither OSM nor OpenHistoricalMap maps it; both terminals placed by hand. APPROXIMATED LEG, Sedgwick Avenue - University Heights (2.1 mi): the Putnam ran here on its own tracks immediately riverward of the Hudson Division along the Harlem River (Fowler: joint stations, separate tracks), and those tracks are gone. So as not to redraw the Hudson Line (metro_north.geojson), this leg is the OSM Hudson Line centreline shifted 25 m to the west (river) side - a schematic parallel, not a surveyed position. The 25 m side and offset are taken from where the surviving Putnam spur at University Heights leaves the Hudson Line (it lies ~25 m west of it); the true spacing further south is unverified. East View - Briarcliff Manor drawn on the PRE-1931 Pocantico Hills (Tarrytown Heights / Tower Hill / Whitson's) alignment, 5.8 mi, chained directly from relation 1376423's members for that grade (Tarrytown Lakes Extension Trail, Red Trail, Greenrock Road, Brothers' Path and Old Railroad Bed Trail carriage roads on the Rockefeller estate, plus razed Putnam Branch ways; one 67 m break bridged). Documented: 6.6 mi (Fowler, East View 20.1 - Briarcliff 26.7) / 6.03 mi abandoned (ICC FD 7563). NOT the 1931 Graham relocation. The 1881 trestle alignment across the Tarrytown Reservoir valley (OSM relation 12946699, ways tagged old_railway_operator='New York City & Northern') was excluded from routing and is not drawn - see metadata. University Heights - East View: Putnam Greenway / Putnam Branch ways / South County Trailway, with the 0.6-mi gap in the relation south of East View (Elmsford) filled by the South County Trailway itself. Briarcliff Manor - Putnam Junction: North County Trailway and Putnam Trailway, ending on the OSM 'Brewster Yard Wye Track' where the Putnam's Y meets the Harlem Division north of Brewster - the Harlem's own track into Brewster station is NOT drawn (it is metro_north.geojson's). No straight-line leg on any of these. LATER ALIGNMENT caveats: the trails follow the LAST alignment; the Croton Lake crossing is drawn on the 1905 bridge built for the New Croton Reservoir (any 1881-1905 approach offset is undated, probably small), and the Middle Branch Reservoir causeway near Carmel is drawn as it survives (no relocation found; reservoir date not checked).

segments.note: New York City and Northern Railroad era. Regular service began April 1881 (xydexx Putnam timeline; Wikipedia); The Sun of May 2, 1881 confirms NYC&N trains at High Bridge and the 155th St transfer to the Sixth Avenue elevated from May 1, 1881. An inaugural special for invited guests ran High Bridge - Brewster on Dec 3, 1880 (The Sun, Dec 4, 1880) - not drawn (one-off special, report recommends against). Ends 1887 with the foreclosure reorganization as the New York and Northern Railway 'late last summer' of 1887 (The Sun, Mar 11, 1888). Until Nov 26, 1881 trains crossed the original East View trestle rather than the Pocantico Hills bypass drawn here (see metadata). Through NY&NE cars 155th St - Hartford via Brewster from May 28, 1882 (xydexx). Headway is an ESTIMATE: no 1880s timetable checked; 120 min is a guess at a handful of trains each way.
sources: Segment-level: The Sun (NY) Dec 4 1880 p.1 and May 2 1881 p.1 for the opening; xydexx timeline and Wikipedia for April 1881; The Sun Mar 11 1888 p.11 for the 1887 reorganization. Headway not sourced.

Ends 1931 on THIS geometry only: the last day of the old route through Tarrytown Heights, Tower Hill and Pocantico Hills was March 15, 1931 (xydexx; Wikipedia), after which trains used the Graham relocation (nyc-putnam-division). Headway is an ESTIMATE: no pre-1951 timetable checked.

segments.note: Putnam Division over the Rockefeller relocation East View - Graham - Briarcliff Manor, built from April 15, 1930 and in use after the old route's last day, March 15, 1931 (xydexx; Graham opened 1931 - Wikipedia). Electric Sedgwick Ave - Van Cortlandt 1926-1943 (Fowler), steam north of there until diesels from July 2, 1951 (xydexx). The Nov 1951 Official Guide Table 90 (New York, Yorktown Heights, Lake Mahopac - Brewster, via High Bridge) is a rail table listing Graham, Elmsford, Carmel, Lake Mahopac and Brewster; its Grand Central times are Hudson Division connections at High Bridge per its own footnotes. Headway is an ESTIMATE: Table 90 shows roughly 7-9 trains each way on weekdays, columns hard to separate in the OCR; 120 min is a round figure from that, not a count.
sources: Segment-level: xydexx timeline and Wikipedia for the 1931 relocation; Official Guide Nov 1951 Table 90 for service in 1951. Headway is an estimate from that table.

segments.note: NYC petitioned to end service in 1956; the PSC refused in May 1957 but allowed a fare rise, and service was cut to about half. Discontinuance approved by PSC order of March 12, 1958 effective June 1; last trains Thursday May 29, 1958 (NYT March 13 and May 30, 1958, cited by Wikipedia). One web summary's 'August 1958' conflicts with the NYT and is disregarded. Freight continued afterwards (oversize loads to 1962, Carmel to 1970, a southern stub into the 1980s) - context only, not drawn. Harlem Division trains kept using Lake Mahopac - Brewster to April 2, 1959 (separate feature). Headway is an ESTIMATE: 'about half' the 1951 service, doubled from 120.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia, citing NYT 1958-03-13 and 1958-05-30, for the 1957 cut and the May 29, 1958 last run. Headway is an estimate.

properties.line: New York Central: Lake Mahopac – Brewster (Harlem Division trains)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, unsourced: carried over from the Putnam Division figure.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 9.8 mi Lake Mahopac (the Harlem crossing, XC) - Putnam Junction against documented c.9.5 mi (Wikipedia: Lake Mahopac 44.38 - Putnam Jct 53.82). Identical to that slice of nyc-putnam-division. Putnam Trailway ways of relation 1376423 to the Brewster Yard Wye Track; no straight-line leg. The Harlem Division's own Lake Mahopac Branch (Golden's Bridge - Lake Mahopac) and its Brewster track are NOT drawn here. The Middle Branch Reservoir causeway is drawn as it survives; no relocation found.

segments.note: After the Putnam main line closed (May 29, 1958), Harlem Division trains running 'around the horn' - Golden's Bridge, the Harlem's Lake Mahopac Branch, then Putnam rails via Mahopac, Carmel and Tilly Foster back to the Harlem at Brewster - kept this slice in passenger use until April 2, 1959 (Wikipedia; a single secondary source, medium confidence). When Harlem trains first ran through this way is not established, so only the year after the main line closed is drawn here (earlier years are already covered by the main-line feature on the same geometry). Headway is an ESTIMATE: no timetable checked. Freight only after April 1959 - not drawn.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia 'New York and Putnam Railroad' (around-the-horn service to April 2, 1959) - single secondary source; not confirmed in a primary timetable or newspaper. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: New York Central: Putnam Division (155th Street – Sedgwick Avenue)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, unsourced: short terminal approach over a swing bridge.
properties.geometry_source: Hand-placed two-point line between the two terminals; no surviving or historical map geometry found.
properties.geometry_quality: APPROXIMATED - the whole 0.3 mi is a straight line 155th Street (Manhattan, el terminal at Eighth Ave, placed by hand) - Sedgwick Avenue (Bronx) on the line of the demolished Putnam Bridge; neither OSM nor OpenHistoricalMap maps it. Documented 0.3 mi (Fowler: 155th St 0.0, Sedgwick Ave 0.3). The Sedgwick end joins the schematic Sedgwick - University Heights leg of the main line (see nyc-putnam-division).

segments.note: NYC&HR/NYC era of the Putnam's original Manhattan terminal: trains from 155th Street (transfer to the Sixth/Ninth Avenue el) over the Putnam Bridge to Sedgwick Avenue, for both the main line and the Getty Square branch. Cut back 1918 when the IRT Ninth Avenue line took over the bridge (Wikipedia station table 'Original terminal from 1881 to 1918'; Fowler '155th Street (cl.1918)'; Wikipedia prose says only 'in the 1910s' - both secondary). After 1918 the bridge carried IRT el trains (Polo Grounds shuttle), which are not Putnam service and not drawn here. Headway is an ESTIMATE: combined main-line and Getty Square trains; not counted.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia NY&P station table and Fowler NYS Railroads (1) sec. 3 for the 1918 cut-back (both secondary); The Evening World Jan 13 1894 / xydexx for the 1894 lease. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: New York and Northern: Getty Square Branch
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, unsourced: short double-track steam branch with close station spacing.
properties.geometry_source: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap (ODbL) relation 1376421 'Yonkers Branch' with opstrace.py; final approach hand-placed.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 3.2 mi Van Cortlandt junction - Getty Square against documented 3.3 mi (Fowler: Van Cortlandt 4.5 - Getty Square 7.8; Wikipedia 3.2-3.4). OSM route relation 1376421 'Yonkers Branch' (old_railway_operator=NYC: abandoned grade, Van Cortlandt Park bridleways, service roads) to its end at Park Hill. APPROXIMATED LEG, Park Hill - Getty Square (0.32 mi): straight line to a hand-placed terminal; the grade into Getty Square is built over and unmapped in OSM and OHM.

segments.note: Built by the Yonkers Rapid Transit Railway (leased to the NYC&N in 1880 but not built until after the 1887 reorganization). First train Saturday March 10, 1888, through from the elevated terminus at 155th Street to Getty Square (The Sun, Mar 11, 1888: 'Rapid transit from the lower portion of New York city to Yonkers became an actual fact yesterday'). An 1883 NYPL map showing the branch is a plan, not service. Ends with the NY&N's 1894 lease to the NYC&HR. Headway is an ESTIMATE: a 'rapid transit' branch through-running to the el; no timetable checked.
sources: Segment-level: The Sun Mar 11 1888 p.11 (opening); The Evening World Jan 13 1894 p.1 / xydexx (1894 lease). Headway not sourced.

properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, unsourced: short double-track branch, steam to 1926 and third-rail electric multiple units 1926-1943.
properties.geometry_source: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap (ODbL) relation 1376421 'Yonkers Branch' with opstrace.py; final approach hand-placed.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 3.2 mi Van Cortlandt junction - Getty Square against documented 3.3 mi (Fowler: Van Cortlandt 4.5 - Getty Square 7.8; Wikipedia 3.2-3.4). segments.note: NYC&HR (lease, Feb 1, 1894) then New York Central. Mosholu station closed 1926; electrified (third rail, Sedgwick Ave - Getty Square) 1926. Abandoned June 30, 1943 (NYT July 1, 1943 p.21 'Getty Square Line Ends; 12 Riders on Last Trip'). CONFLICT: Fowler heads the section 'electrified 1926>1942' - read as a slip; the dated NYT story is taken. Yonkers fought the abandonment to the US Supreme Court, which let it stand; rails lifted Dec 1944 (NYT 1944-11-14, 1944-12-09). Headway is an ESTIMATE: no timetable checked.
sources: Segment-level: The Evening World Jan 13 1894 p.1 / xydexx (lease); NYT 1943-07-01 p.21 via Wikipedia (end). Fowler's 1942 conflicts and is recorded, not used. Headway not sourced.
